memory_update.text: AXTI should remain the primary underfollowed direct-substrate candidate for this node because SEC filings explicitly connect InP substrates to hyperscale, AI, silicon-photonics and PIC applications and describe a very small primary-supplier base.

VECO should be tracked as an upstream equipment/capacity-constraint candidate for InP laser manufacturing rather than as a substrate supplier; evidence focus should be order quality, customer identity, backlog conversion and exposure size.

LITE and COHR validate demand pull into InP-based optical components for 800G/1.6T and CPO, but they are less pure for the substrate chokepoint and should mainly serve as reference or near-reference anchors.

Layer 2 should verify market caps, analyst coverage, 2025-2026 segment revenue, customer concentration, China/export-control risk, and whether InP/GaAs substrate tightness is independently confirmed by primary filings or customer qualification disclosures.

node: Compound substrates and precision materials for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers and co-packaged optics
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the compound-substrate and precision-materials chokepoint behind AI data-center optical links. The highest-relevance underfollowed name is AXTI because it directly supplies InP/GaAs/Ge substrates and its 2024 10-K explicitly links InP to data-center, hyperscale, AI, silicon-photonics and PIC applications while stating that the InP substrate market has only three primary suppliers including AXT. Adjacent picks-and-shovels exposure appears in VECO, which sells MOCVD, wet-processing and ion-beam tools for InP laser manufacturing. LITE and COHR are included as higher-attention reference/near-reference optical-component leaders because their InP laser, 800G/1.6T and CPO exposure helps validate demand pull through the substrate and epiwafer chain. No candidate here is a recommendation; all are Layer 1 research candidates requiring customer, margin, capacity, and concentration verification.
